transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I'm here because of my house. Everyone keeps acting like this foreclosure is just about paperwork and missed payments, but... I know that's not true. I know the bank, the loan servicer, and even some people at my job have been quietly working together to push me out of my home. They can show me all the papers they want, but it doesn't change what I've been seeing going on for almost two years now.
Do you think these people are working together against you specifically, or is it more about the house itself?

I'm not entirely sure. I mean... it's my house, so it definitely feels like it's against me personally. But whether they targeted me specifically from the start, or if they just really want the property and I'm just in the way... I don't know. I haven't figured that part out. I just know what I've seen them doing, and they are definitely working together to get me out.
Do you think there are other people or groups that are out to harm you, beyond those involved with your house?

No, I... no. It's really just the people connected to the house. I don't have any reason to think anyone else is after me or trying to hurt me or anything like that. Outside of this whole mortgage and foreclosure situation, my life is pretty normal. I haven't noticed anyone else acting strange or coming after me. It's strictly just this one specific issue with my property and the people trying to take it.
Do you think the beliefs you have about your house and the people involved are thoughts that most people would understand and agree with, or are they something that might seem unusual to others?

I... well, I suppose it might sound a little unusual to other people. If you're just looking at it from the outside, you know, it probably just looks like a regular foreclosure. I get why someone would think that. Most people just trust what the bank puts on paper. 

But... they aren't the ones living it. They aren't seeing the things I'm seeing, or noticing how the people at my job are acting. So, sure, maybe a lot of people wouldn't understand it or agree with me right away because they just don't have all the pieces. But I know what's actually happening, even if it sounds strange to someone else.
How long have you been thinking that there's a conspiracy involving the bank, loan servicer, and people at your job to take your house?

It's been going on for about a year and nine months now. That's when all of this really started... when the foreclosure notices began showing up in the mail, and the constant bank calls just started completely taking over our home life. So, yeah, right around a year and nine months.
Have you developed a clear explanation or theory about how all these people and organizations are working together against you?

I... no, I don't really know exactly how they're doing it. I don't know how they communicate with each other or what goes on behind closed doors. 

I just know what I see happening. I don't have some big theory about, you know, how the bank is actually getting in touch with the people at my job. I just know that they are involved because of the things they say and how they act around me. The actual details of how they coordinate it all or who is pulling the strings... I really couldn't tell you. I just know that it's happening.
How certain are you that your beliefs about the conspiracy to take your house are true?

I'm completely certain. I know everyone keeps acting like this foreclosure is just paperwork, you know, just missed payments and standard procedure. But no amount of papers they show me changes what I've been seeing for almost two years now. I know the bank, the loan servicer, and the people at my job have been quietly working together to push me out of my house. I don't need to know how they do it to know that it's the truth.
Have your beliefs about the conspiracy to take your house changed at all since they first started?

No, they haven't changed at all. Like I was just saying, everyone keeps acting like this foreclosure is just paperwork and missed payments, but I know what's really going on. I know the bank, the loan servicer, and even the people at my job have been quietly working together to push me out of my house. That hasn't changed since day one. No amount of papers they try to show me changes what I’ve been seeing for almost two years now.
Are your beliefs about the conspiracy affecting your ability to work or interact with people outside of the situation with your house?

No, not really. I mean, when it doesn't have to do with the foreclosure, I'm fine. I still get up every day and go to work. I supervise my team at the store, I handle the schedules, deal with customer complaints... I take care of myself just fine. 

It's really only when... well, the problems only start when I get certain mail, or if the bank calls, or if there's paperwork at my job that seems tied to the house situation. That's when it affects me. But outside of that? I function perfectly normally.
You mentioned that you see things happening that make you believe in the conspiracy, can you describe one of these specific events that you think is evidence of the conspiracy?

I mean... I'm not sure I can give you just one specific event. It doesn't really work like that. 

I haven't been keeping a list of specific things or, you know, writing down dates to point to. It's more just... the whole way they've been handling everything over the last two years. I don't really have one single moment or a specific piece of evidence I can just hand you, if that's what you mean. It's just what I've been seeing happen all along.
Have you ever had any moments where you doubted your beliefs about the conspiracy to take your house?

No, I really haven't. Like I said earlier, I'm here because everyone keeps acting like this foreclosure is just normal paperwork and missed payments, but I know what's actually happening. I know the bank, the loan servicer, and the people at my job have been quietly working together to push me out of my house. So, no, I don't doubt it. No amount of papers they try to show me changes what I’ve been seeing for almost two years. I know what I know.
Have you changed your daily routines or behaviors in any way because of your beliefs about the conspiracy?

No, not really. I mean, I haven't started doing anything weird or different, if that's what you're asking. I just go to work, come home, do my grocery shopping... just normal things. I don't hide in my house or take different routes to work or anything like that. I just live my life the same way I always have. The only thing I do is pay close attention to any mail or calls from the bank, but that's just common sense when you know they're trying to pull something. Other than that, my routine is exactly the same.
Do you feel anxious, depressed, or significantly upset when you think about the conspiracy to take your house?

No, I wouldn't say I feel depressed or anxious about it. I mean, it's frustrating, obviously. Anyone would be annoyed if people were actively working behind their back to force them out of their home. But I don't sit around crying about it or anything like that. I just go to work and keep doing what I need to do. It makes me mad sometimes, just knowing what they're trying to pull, but I'm not depressed over it.
Do you believe the people involved in the conspiracy against you have any supernatural or extraordinary abilities?

No, of course not. They don't have superpowers or anything like that. They're just regular people—bank managers, HR people, loan officers. They just have access to the system and the paperwork, so they know how to manipulate things from the inside. There's nothing supernatural about it at all. It's just... well, normal corruption, I guess you'd call it. They're just using their jobs to try and force me out. I don't think they're reading my mind or using magic or anything crazy like that.
Do you think the bank, loan servicer, and people at your job are working together against you in a way that's impossible or extremely unlikely in real life?

No, I don't think it's impossible at all. I mean, everyone keeps acting like this foreclosure is just about standard paperwork and missed payments. But I know the bank, the loan servicer, and even people at my job have been quietly working together to push me out of my house. It's not some unlikely, crazy plot, it's just what they are actually doing. And honestly, no amount of papers they try to show me is going to change what I’ve been seeing with my own eyes for almost two years now.
Have you ever had a period of time where you didn't think about the conspiracy against you for several days in a row?

No, not really. I mean, it's my home, so... it's kind of hard to just forget about it. I don't think a single day goes by without it crossing my mind, let alone several days in a row. You can't really just ignore something like this when people are actively trying to pull the rug out from under you. I have to stay on top of what they're doing, or they'll get away with it. So, no, I haven't had a break from thinking about it.
Have you ever considered the possibility that your beliefs about the conspiracy might be incorrect?

No. I mean, like I was saying a minute ago, everyone wants to act like this is just about missed payments and standard paperwork. They want me to think I'm wrong. But I'm not. I know for a fact that the bank, the loan servicer, and the people at my job have been quietly working together to push me out of my house. 

I've been watching them do it for almost two years now. So, no, I don't consider that my beliefs might be incorrect, because no amount of papers they try to show me is going to change what I know is actually happening.
Have you ever had a time when you didn't believe in the conspiracy against you, even if just for a short period?

No, I haven't. I mean, why would I? I'm only here because everyone keeps acting like this foreclosure is just some routine paperwork issue or about missed payments. But I know what's really going on. 

I know the bank, the loan servicer, and those people at my job have been quietly working together to push me out of my house. I've been seeing it happen for almost two years. So, no, there hasn't been a time where I didn't believe it, because it's the truth. No amount of papers they try to show me is going to change what I know they're doing.
Do you think the bank, loan servicer, and people at your job are using any unusual or bizarre methods to try and take your house?

No, not really. I mean, I don't know what you mean by bizarre, but they aren't doing anything... crazy. It's just paperwork and lying. 

The bank will say they lost my payment, or the servicer changes a due date, and the people at my job... they just mess with my schedule so my paychecks are short. It's all very normal, everyday stuff. They're just using the system against me. So, no, nothing unusual like that. It's just a coordinated effort to ruin me.
